newsitem.title: MEXICO: Partial accord reached in Mexico Chiapas talks.
newsitem.headline: Partial accord reached in Mexico Chiapas talks.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1996-10-23

text.p: Mediators took a first step toward reviving peace talks in Mexico's troubled southern state of Chiapas on Tuesday, hammering out an accord on one of five demands by Zapatista rebels, a legislator said.

Jose Narro Cespedes, spokesman for a legislative committee on Chiapas, told reporters in this Chiapas City that agreement had been reached after several days of talks for a watchdog Verification Commission to be set up to make sure peace accords between the rebels and the government are implemented.
The establishment of such a commission was one of five Zapatista conditions for returning to full peace talks with the government of President Ernesto Zedillo.
The full talks have been suspended since early September.
Narro, of the tiny Labour Party, said more details of the commission would be announced on Wednesday.
The agreement was thrashed out in talks between the rebels, the legislative commission and mediators led by Chiapas bishop Samuel Ruiz.

The Zapatista rebels, mostly Maya Indians but led by the charismatic, non-indigenous Subcommander Marcos, are also demanding the replacement of the government negotiating team and freedom for Zapatista prisoners before it will resume full talks.

The rebels rose up in arms on New Year's Day 1994 to demand indigenous rights and greater democracy. At least 145 people died in the early days of the rebellion but there has been almost no fighting since.
